newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday December 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday December 17.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Ruling centre-left Olive Tree coalition and opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance reach agreement on extension of broadcasting licences until end of May next year with possible extension beyond that providing bill is approved by at least one house of parliament. Communist Refoundation party says it won't vote for the accord. (All)

* Former Milan anti-graft magistrate and ex-minister Antonio Di Pietro exercises right not to speak as witness in trial of Paolo Berlusconi, brother of former prime minister Silvio. Di Pietro accuses former prime minister Bettino Craxi of ordchestrating a campaign to ruin him. (All)

* International Monetary Fund inspectors tell Italian government it must reform pensions sector and welfare spending and carry out extra budget measures for 13-14 trillion lire in 1997 if it wants to enter single European currency at start. (All)
* Treasury to pay state holding IRI at least 14.53 trillion lire to take over its controlling stake in state telcoms holding Stet. (All)

* EU Commissioner Karel Van Miert will present a report to the Commission on Wednesday recommending a December deadline for reduction of Iri debts be extended until June 30, 1997 on four conditions: privatisation of Autostrade; privatisation of Finmare and sale of Banca di Roma stake; sale of Stet stake to Treasury for around 11.2 trillion lire; privatisation of Seat.

* British Telecommunications chief executive Peter Bonham says BT is not interested in Italian GSM service operator Omnitel but wants to compete for third PCN phone service licence when it is tendered. Also says BT is not interested in Stet although it might be interested in other state telecom concerns like Seat. (Repubblica, Il Sole)
* U.S. telecoms group Bell Atlantic exercises right to buy additional 8.26 percent stake in Italy's mobile phone group Omnitel, scuppering German group Mannesmann's hopes of purchase.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
